title: Mental illness as a ground for divorce - evidentiary requirements
p1:
Can a diagnosis alone decide a divorce case? Many people assume it can, but the law often looks deeper than a medical label.

Mental illness and divorce involve more than simply proving that someone has a condition.
p2:
A common misconception is that any mental health issue automatically becomes a legal ground for divorce. The reality is that courts usually focus on factors like the severity of the condition, its impact on the marriage, and whether the evidence shows the required legal standard.

A surprising point: medical records alone may not always be enough. Testimony, expert opinions, treatment history, and proof of how the condition affects marital life can become crucial.
p3:
The key lesson is that divorce cases involving mental illness are decided on evidence, not assumptions or stigma. A person’s diagnosis does not define their ability to maintain a relationship, and each case depends on its specific facts.

Strong evidence tells the real story behind the legal claim.
